NATIONAL FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 3 ) which is identical with ISO 16589-3:2001 `Rotary shaft lip-type seals incorporating thermoplastic sealing elements -- Part 3: Storage, handling and installation' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendations of the Basic Fluid Power Sectional Committee and approval of the Medical Instruments, General and Production Engineering Division Council. Rotary shaft lip-type seals are used to retain fluid in equipment where the differential pressure is relatively low. Typically, the shaft rotates and the housing is stationary, although in some applications the shaft is stationary and the housing rotates. Dynamic sealing is normally the result of a designed element incorporated in the seal. interference fit between the shaft and a flexible

Similarly, a designed interference fit between the outside diameter housing bore retains the seal and prevents static leakage. Careful storage, handling to and during installation,

1

Scope
from suitably formulated compounds, based on

ISO 16589 describes seals utilizing sealing elements manufactured thermoplastic materials, such as polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE). NOTE

ISO 16589 is complementary to ISO6194 which covers elastomeric seals. of the seals.

This part of ISO 16589 gives users guidance on the careful storage, handling and proper installation Attention is drawn to the hazards involved and to ways of avoiding them.

references

3

Terms and definitions

For the purposes of this part of ISO 16589, the terms and definitions given in ISO 5598 and ISO 16589-2 apply.

4

General storage

4.1 Rotary shaft lip-type seals shall be stored with caution because the service life of bearings and/or other costly machined parts may depend on how well the lip seal performs. Hazards which maybe encountered include: -- . -- . . temperature (see 4.2), ,.. ,

humidity (see 4.2), radioactive materials (see 4.6), fumes (see 4.6), insects (see 4.7),

The storage area shall be kept at a temperature

40 "/0 to 70 ?40.
4.3 During sunlight. 4.4 storage, rubber-coated or semi-rubber-covered seals shall be protected against light, especially

Seals shall be stored on a "first in, first out" basis for stock rotation purposes only.

4.5 Rotary shaft seals incorporating thermoplastic sealing elements can be supplied assembled on mandrels for ease of transport and storage. These mandrels have the advantage of protecting the sealing lip and preventing relaxation of the lip, which could result in increased interference. When this is the case, the seals shall remain on mandrels until immediately prior to installation. In some cases, the seals are supplied with individual mandrels that can be used as assembly tools.
NOTE The seal manufacturer should ensure that the seal/seals are assembled onto mandrels backside first, unless

individual mandrels are supplied. The user should withdraw the seal from the mandrel backside first. 4.6 4.7 Seals shall be protected from radioactive materials and fumes that can cause deterioration Seals shall be protected from insects and rodents. of the seal.

4.8 Lip seals should preferably be stored in a place other than a work area to avoid possible mechanical damage by equipment or falling objects. A closed container will provide protection from mechanical damage, as well as from dust, grit and other contaminants. 4.9 When cartons excessive weight. of lip seals are stacked, care shall be taken to avoid damage to the lower seals due to

5

Packaging
to the user

5.1 The product shall be protected from damage and foreign material en route from the manufacturer and during storage.

NOTE Several methods are used to package lip seals. Good commercial practice dictates that the best packaging is the least expensive which still affords the protection desired. This should be assessed and agreed on by the vendor and customar for each part shipped.

5.2 During unpacking, care shall be exercised so as not to cut or tear the seal element with sharp instruments, such as knives, screwdrivers, etc., brought about by improperly unpacking bulk packs, roll packs and individuatty wrapped or boxed packs. Seals should not be removed from their packaging until they are ready for installation. This method will ensure NOTE better protection and identication.

6

Handling of loose parts

6.1 After seals have been removed from thek packaging, they shall be handled carefully to prevent damage prior to installation. It shall be borne in mind that seal lips are extremely vulnerable to damage and that the smallest niok can provide a potential leak path.
NOTE Small nicks can even be caused by a fingernail.

2

IS ISO

15545

(Part 3):2004

16589-3:2001

6.2 Seals should never be threaded on wires or string, or be hung on nails or pegs. Mishandling can lead to the lip being distorted or even cut. 6.3 Care shall be exercised when handling seals which may damage other seals, especially come into contact with sealing edges. 6.4 The seal surfaces shall be free of grit, chips and other abrasives.

seals in this way

if metal edges can

6.5 If it becomes necessary to clean the lip seals, the manufacturer shall be requested to recommend cleaning solution, e.g. dry-cleaning benzine or alcohol if the contact period is short. Abrasive cleaners shall never be used on lip seals as they can remove thermoplastic flat spots and operating deficiencies.

a suitable

material and metal, causing

Improper solutions which can also cause a breakdown in the rubber/thermoplastic/metal elements and case or damage the metal case shall not be used. In case of doubt as to the compatibility of the cleaning solution, the manufacturer

bond

between

the

of the seal should be contacted.

7.1 7.2 7.3

Seal installation
The seal shall be examined before installation to ensure that it is clean and undamaged. onto the shaft unlubricated, unless otherwise specified by the supplier.

The sealing lip can be assembled

The sealing lip, normally, shall face the fluid to be sealed. as specified

The end of the shaft and the mouth of the housing bore shall be provided with lead-in chamfers 7.4 in ISO 16589-1.

7.5 The seal shall always be aligned with a machined surface to ensure installed squareness. Typical installation assembly tools designed for this purpose shall be used (see Figures 1 and 2). Unfinished surfaces cannot be used because of the danger of misalignment of the seal. 7.6 Care shall be taken pressure. not to deform the seal case during the installation process by applying excessive

7.7 Any surfaces over which the seal lip has to slide during installation spots.

shall be smooth and free from rough

7.8 Bullet-nosed assembly tools, of the type illustrated in Figure 3, provide a large lead-in chamfer to facilitate installation of the seal onto a shaft. Figure 4 illustrates a bullet which is used to prevent seal lip damage if it slides over splines, keyways, holes or other sharp edges. 7.9 The special bullet-nosed assembly tool shown in Figure 4 prevents installation of the seal over holes, splines or keyways in the shaft. dam'age to the sealing lip during

7.10 If press-fitted components have to be forced over the running area of the seal, the shaft diameter should be reduced by 0,2 mm in the running area. The patilcular rotary shaft lip-type seal designed for the shaft maybe used without any negative effect on the sealing action. See Figure 5. 7.11 When using rubber-covered seals, the outside surface shall be lubricated with a suitable lubricant to facilitate entry into the housing. Assembly into the housing shall be carried out by pressing with uniform speed and pressure to the assembled position and holding briefly to prevent any spring back. 7.12 If seals have to be assembled at very low temperatures; flexibility of the sealing lip may be restored heating the seal for 10 min to 15 min at a temperature not exceeding 30 "C. 7.13 In the case of replacement, a new rotary shaft lip-type seal shall always be used. by

3

IS 15545 (Part 3):2004 ISO 16589-3:2001

The sealing lip of the new seal shall not be allowed to engage with the previous track of rotation; it shall be shifted to the fluid side. This can be achieved by fitting spacers or exchanging the shaft bushes or the race rings or by

varying the depth to which the seal is pressed into the bore.
The sealing surfaces (shaft and bore) shall be thoroughly

cleaned, care being taken not to damage them.

NOTE 1 Reusable bullet-nosed tools should not be allowed to become damaged, otherwise they will cause lip damage. Soft metals, such as aluminium, should not be used for this purpose, NOTE 2 Disposable plastic tools can be used to advantage in some applications.
